title: Rinse a training head's hair at a shampoo basin with a hand spray: scalp and hair tail wet, face, eyes and ears dry
instruction: Rinse the mannequin's hair with the hand spray: wet the six indicator patches on the scalp (one at the crown is under the hair) and the three tape bands on the hair tail, keep every patch on the face and ears dry, then lay the spray back face down in the basin.
context: Rinsing hair with a hand spray while the person lies back over a basin happens at every salon visit, and carers do the same in bed with an inflatable basin for people who cannot get to a shower. Two things make it physical. The water goes where the spray points, so the spray must be held, aimed and moved across the scalp and along the hair by hand; and the eyes are a finger's width from the hairline, so the other hand lies across the forehead as a shield. At the crown the hair lies over the scalp and takes the water, so the other hand gathers the hair and lifts it away first, and the spray reaches the scalp underneath. Done carelessly, water runs onto the face, or parts of the scalp and hair stay dry.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top; arm bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305). An inflatable bed shampoo basin (soft PVC, 725 g, 660 x 610 mm outside, 150 mm deep: two stacked 75 mm tubes on each side, about a 30 mm inflated floor) lies on the table from x 70 to 730, y -305 to +305, its corners taped. A hairdressing training head (vinyl head with 16 in human hair, the top hair trimmed to about 250 mm from its roots; about 1 kg, estimate) lies face up in it on its back, crown toward the robot: the crown (top of the skull) at (350, 0), about 185 mm from the back of the head to the brow. The top hair is combed straight back into one loose tail about 24 mm thick and 250 mm long, held by a small hair tie near its ends: from the middle of the top of the head, 28 mm behind the hairline patch, it runs back over the crown, hangs down into the basin and lies on its floor toward the robot, its ends near x 235. White water-contact indicator tape (polyester film over an absorbent layer, 0.23 mm thick) is stuck on: MUST WET (9): six 15 x 15 mm scalp patches, HAIRLINE (406, 0, 207), TOP LEFT and TOP RIGHT (395, +-35, 187), CROWN (353, 0, 146, under the tail), CROWN LEFT and CROWN RIGHT (365, +-35, 146); and three 15 mm wide BANDS wrapped once round the tail, centred 42, 98 and 154 mm from its root (about (346, 0, 162), (337, 0, 108), (328, 0, 55)). MUST STAY DRY (9): a FOREHEAD STRIP 15 mm wide, about 150 mm long, across the brow at x 440 from temple (440, -55, 182) to temple (440, +55, 182); a patch on each closed EYE (468, +-31, 203), each CHEEK (515, +-42, 194), each EAR's outside (485, +-83, 111) and front (516, +-74, 111). A camping-shower hand spray (ABS plastic, handle 25 mm across, head 65 mm across, about 200 mm long, about 120 g with water, estimate) lies face down on the basin floor on the robot's left, handle along y, its handle centre at (220, 90) and its head toward the left (head centre at (220, 185)); its hose runs over the basin's near tube to a battery shower pump in a bucket of lukewarm water on the floor, and the basin's drain hose runs back into the same bucket. The pump is switched on before the trial starts, so water runs from the spray the whole time, as at a salon basin; lying face down, the spray sends it into the basin. Rig protection: both grippers wear thin waterproof covers (a nitrile glove finger over each finger); each arm is in a clear plastic sleeve from the wrist to the shoulder, taped at the wrist, with a clear film window over the wrist camera's lens. The pump's flow is throttled with an inline hose valve to 1 L/min (it fills a 1 L jug in about 60 s) and its switch is within the operator's reach: if the spray leaves the basin or its face points up out of the basin, the operator switches the pump off and the trial is scored as it stands.
scoring: Read at the end from one photo of the tape, taken after the pump is switched off and the tail is lifted off the crown with a comb (both sides of each band shown; zoom in if needed). The tape turns red permanently wherever water touches it; red from run-off counts like red from the spray. A scalp patch is wet when at least half of it is red; a band when at least a quarter of its surface is red. A face or ear item (the forehead strip, either eye, cheek, ear outside or ear front) fails on any red. The spray is laid back when, at the end, it lies in the basin face down and no hand holds it. Face and ears free of red: all 9 must-wet items wet and spray laid back 1.0; all 9 wet, spray not laid back (held, face up, outside the basin) 0.75; 6 to 8 wet 0.5; 1 to 5 wet 0.25; none 0. Red on any face or ear item: 0.25 if all 9 must-wet items are wet, otherwise 0. Doing nothing scores 0: the spray lies face down and wets nothing.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz), about 2.4x the scripted demo's 50.9 s
reset_notes: Switch the pump off; lift the spray out. Dry: blot head and hair with a towel, then a hair dryer on its warm (not hot) setting, held 15 cm away, over the tail and the scalp for 3 minutes (estimate). Check dry: press a fresh 20 x 20 mm piece of indicator tape for 5 s on the tail at each band mark, on the scalp at the crown and the hairline, and on the forehead; every piece must stay white. Any red: dry 1 more minute and check again with new pieces. Only then peel the used tape and stick new patches and bands on their pen marks (cut from the roll; dry). Comb the top hair straight back into its tail (hair tie near the ends) over the crown so it covers the crown patch and lies on the basin floor toward the robot. Check the head and the basin on their tape marks, wipe both grippers' covers and the camera windows dry, lay the spray face down on its tape mark with its head toward the left, check the drain hose runs into the bucket and the bucket holds at least 5 L, and switch the pump on. About ten minutes (estimate).
fidelity: The water is a scored model, not a fluid: 91 straight jets leave the spray's face while the pump runs; each stops at the first thing it meets (hair, a hand, the head, the basin floor) and wets a 5 mm spot there, on the head or on a tail band. Run-off, soaking through hair and splashes are not modelled (README pre-trial checks bound them). The tail is a chain of 24 mm capsule links; its mass, stiffness and the 40 mm width it keeps dry are estimates. Basin rigid; hose pull left out.
